== Biography ==
Peter Glasgow was born on 1 Jul 1829 in Aberlady, East Lothian, Scotland, son of [[Glasgow-160|Thomas Glasgow]]  and [[Burns-2926|Euphemia (Burns) Glasgow]].

In the 1841 census Peter (age 12) was in Ballencrieff, Aberlady, East Lothian.<ref>
'''1841 Census''':
"1841 Scotland Census"<br/>
Parish: Aberlady; ED: 2; Page: 4; Line: 555; Year: 1841<br/>
{{Ancestry Record|1004|818051|au}} (accessed 5 February 2022)<br/>
Peter Glasgow (12) in Ballencrieff, Aberlady, East Lothian. Born in East Lothian, Scotland.
</ref>

In the 1851 census Peter (age 21), Rail Lab, was the lodger of David Brownlee at 3 Comely Green Place, Leith South, Midlothian.<ref>
'''1851 Census''':
"1851 Scotland Census"<br/>
Parish: Leith South; ED: 11A; Page: 1; Line: 20; Roll: CSSCT1851_189; Year: 1851<br/>
{{Ancestry Record|1076|2768909|au}} (accessed 5 February 2022)<br/>
Peter Glasgow (21) lodger, Rail Lab, in household of David Brownlee (25) in 3 Comely Green Place, Leith South, Midlothian.
</ref>

Peter married [[Bryden-65|Jane Bryden]] on 4 Mar 1856 in Newbury, Ontario, Canada.<ref>[https://scholar.uwindsor.ca/swoda-windsor-region/70  J. H. Beers & Co., "Commemorative Biographical Record of the County of Kent Ontario" (1904). SWODA: Windsor & Region Publications. 70.]
Peter Glasgow Page 144</ref>

In the 1861 census Peter (age 31) was the married head of household in Mosa, Middlesex, Canada West.<ref>

Peter Glasgow (31), married head of household in Mosa, Middlesex, Canada West. Born in Upper Canada.
</ref>

'''1911 Census''':

Peter died on 24 May 1916 in Camden, Ontario aged 86.<ref>{{FindAGrave|	64836615|sameas=yes}}</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-160]] is assessed at 86% (probable). Peter’s biography names Thomas and Euphemia, with an 1829 Aberlady birth immediately after their 1828 marriage. The 1904 Kent County life account and 1841 local census supply coherent context, but the held 1841 citation gives no relationship and the parent passage is not transcribed.

Held citation and associated narrative supports this specific paternal assessment; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Read the p.144 parental passage and Peter’s 1829 baptism.

Source basis already held: [https://scholar.uwindsor.ca/swoda-windsor-region/70 J. H. Beers & Co., "Commemorative Biographical Record of the County of Kent Ontario" (1904). SWODA: Windsor & Region Publications. 70. (https://scholar.uwindsor.ca/swoda-windsor-region/70) Peter Glasgow Page 144]; [https://scholar.uwindsor.ca/swoda-windsor-region/70 J. H. Beers & Co., "Commemorative Biographical Record of the County of Kent Ontario" (1904). SWODA: Windsor & Region Publications. 70. (https://scholar.uwindsor.ca/swoda-windsor-region/70) Peter Glasgow Page 144]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
